title: task complete succeeds with unchecked acceptance criteria / definition of done -- undocumented, likely intended, needs a durable line
description:
Reported inbound by quest-web via the orchestrator: created a task with an unchecked acceptance criterion, ran task complete, and it succeeded with the AC still checked: false -- no block, no warning, no diagnostic. The orchestrator asked for a ruling (defect, intended, or enforcement on an unexercised path) before questgraph.dev's public copy asserts anything about gate enforcement.

Established by direct source investigation, not inference from behavior alone:

1. Zero enforcement exists anywhere in src/ tying acceptanceCriteria or definitionOfDone (same shape, same question, DoD wasn't separately tested by quest-web but shares the identical code path) to a completion/transition check. Confirmed by reading TasksService.complete() (tasks.ts ~635) and the domain transitionTask() (domain/tasks/tasks.ts ~437) line by line, plus an exhaustive grep for '.checked' across src/ -- every hit is schema validation of the checked:boolean type or migration pass-through, never a completion gate.

2. transitionTask() DOES gate the terminal transition on something: blockingGatesSatisfied(...) over the task's gates/gateEvents -- a structurally SEPARATE field from acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone. This is reading (3) from the report, but it applies only to gates, not to acceptance criteria -- see the companion task filed alongside this one, because gates itself turns out to have no CLI write path (same shape as QCLI-251).

3. My ruling: most likely INTENDED (reading 2), not a defect -- but this is an inference from adjacent philosophy text, not a confirmed engineering decision, and I'm saying so plainly rather than overclaiming certainty. This project's own task-finalization agent-instructions (quest instructions task-finalization) already state the philosophy explicitly: 'An acceptance criterion you cannot prove stays unchecked, and the reason belongs in the notes... A criterion checked on faith is worse than one left open, because it stops anyone else from looking.' That describes and endorses closing a task with an honestly-unchecked criterion -- the tool's role is to record truthfully what was proven, not to force a closer to lie about completeness by ticking boxes to get past a gate. No ADR, spec, or code comment establishes this as a deliberate CLI-enforcement decision, though -- it is absent by omission, not by a documented choice.

4. The gap the orchestrator flagged either way: quest task complete --help (command-help.ts) says only 'Move a task to its terminal complete status' -- nothing about acceptance criteria being advisory. The natural assumption on seeing an acceptance-criteria field with a checked flag is that something enforces it before closure; nothing here corrects that assumption anywhere a caller would actually look.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A design decision is confirmed (not just inferred): acceptance criteria and definition-of-done stay advisory at completion by design, or quest task complete should refuse/warn on unchecked items -- record which, and why, durably (an ADR or a spec note, not just a task record)

quest task complete --help and command-help.ts state plainly whether unchecked acceptance criteria/definition-of-done block completion, so the natural assumption someone forms from seeing the field is corrected at the point they would look

If advisory is confirmed as the decision: task view / task list --json surfaces unchecked-criteria-at-completion as a visible signal (e.g. in the completed record, or in doctor/overview) rather than only in the raw checked:false state someone has to know to look for

If enforcement is decided instead: quest task complete gains a way to refuse or require an explicit override (e.g. --force) when acceptance criteria or definition-of-done remain unchecked, matching the existing blocking-gate pattern in transitionTask
